the PC lobe of the terrestrial slug, Limax maximus, contains a coupled network of bursting neurons that can generate oscillatory electrical activity.
Ca2+ action potentials propagate in the PC lode at different rates in two different morphological types of bursting neurons.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ca2+ plays a central role in the initiation of action potentials and the propagation of action potentials along the axon.
Ca2+ action potentials are initiated in the apical dendrites and propagate in an all-or-none fashion down the apical dendrite, along the axon and up the basal dendrite of the bursting neuron.
calcium-dependent action potentials are initiated at the axon hillock of the bursting neurons and then propagate in the axon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the initiation of the calcium-dependent action potential in the PC lube is due to a combination of a calcium-dependent inward current and a voltage-dependent outward current.

the initiation of action potential in a bursting neuron is triggered by a calcium-dependent inward current and that this current is initiated by a calcium wave that propagates from the cell body to the neurites.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the propagation of action potentials in the PC lobo occurs via a mechanism that depends on calcium, and that the propagation velocity in the two types of bursting cells is different.
the initiation and propagation of action potentials in bursting neurons is calcium dependent.
